correction: Earlier attribution of the R3 A2 death to a Windows AppHang was invalid. Available WER AppHang/AppCrash timestamps do not overlap the validation window. The observed -1 therefore cannot currently be classified as native crash, OS kill, self-exit, or parent termination from existing evidence.
purpose: Make the next child disappearance attributable without changing M5 gameplay/network semantics or retry behavior.
authorized_changes: Spawn M5 child Godot processes directly with OS.execute_with_pipe(..., false) instead of OS.create_process so stdout/stderr remain attached to the real child PID with no shell wrapper.
Continuously drain stdout and stderr into per-child files so output exists even if the child dies before creating its JSON report or Godot --log-file.

Record per-child lifecycle JSON: pid, label, spawn timestamp, stdout/stderr paths, result path, observed running/dead transitions, actual get_process_exit_code value, parent_kill_requested flag, parent kill reason/timestamp, last result JSON, and last control JSON snapshot.
When a wait detects a dead child, include the lifecycle record in the returned failure report.
Before parent cleanup OS.kill, durably mark parent_kill_requested=true and the cleanup reason.
Add contract guards requiring direct pipe spawn, exit-code capture, and parent-kill attribution.
honesty_boundary: R4 may prove NOT_PARENT_INITIATED termination when no parent kill was requested, but without WER dump/debugger it must not claim SELF_EXIT versus EXTERNAL_TERMINATE.
get_process_exit_code=-1 must be recorded literally; on Windows the API is implemented, but -1 alone is not sufficient to assign root cause.
R4 is diagnostic instrumentation, not by itself a correctness fix. Even a 10/10 R4 run does not erase the preserved R3 failure.
non_goals: Do not change convergence, LEAVE, Item Graph, networking or SM1 runtime semantics.
Do not enable WER LocalDumps automatically because that mutates host registry outside repository scope.
acceptance_r4: M5 contracts pass with observability guards.
A child that exits before report creation leaves non-empty stdout/stderr capture files if it emitted any bytes and always leaves a lifecycle JSON.
Dead-child failure report contains pid, label, actual exit_code, parent_kill_requested, wait_label, last_result and last_control.
Parent cleanup kills are explicitly distinguishable from non-parent-initiated exits.
Run the diagnostic stability gate only on the new R4 candidate; stop on first failure and preserve evidence.
escalation_rule: If R4 captures a non-parent-initiated A2 exit, classify from stdout/stderr + exit code. If still ambiguous and reproducible on Windows, enable WER LocalDumps manually or attach debugger before an R5 protocol/runtime repair. If parent_kill_requested=true unexpectedly, fix the parent lifecycle path before any network changes.
